input: Find bribery and corruption cases involving Trafigura

entity.group: Trafigura Group. The Singapore-registered Trafigura Group Pte. Ltd. has been the group's consolidating entity since FY2015, replacing the Dutch company Trafigura Beheer B.V. Trafigura Beheer B.V. is still the group entity named in the US and Swiss bribery cases.

events.jurisdiction: United States (DOJ; federal court, court not named on the page opened)
events.amount: More than USD 126m in total (as of 2024-03-29): criminal fine of about USD 80.4m plus forfeiture of about USD 46.5m. Up to about USD 27m of the fine is credited against payments to Brazilian authorities. DOJ puts the profit from the scheme at more than USD 61m.
events.summary: Trafigura Beheer pleaded guilty to conspiring to violate the FCPA anti-bribery provisions by paying bribes to Petrobras officials from about 2003 to 2014, including up to 20 cents per barrel from 2009, hidden through shell companies and offshore accounts. DOJ also criticised the company's early cooperation, including late preservation and production of documents.

events.type: Bribery of a foreign public official (Angola / Sonangol) and corporate failure to prevent bribery
events.status: convicted at first instance; not final, appeals announced
events.parties: Trafigura Beheer BV (company); Mike Wainwright, former COO (32 months, 20 suspended); Thierry Plojoux, former Trafigura employee and intermediary; Paulo Gouveia Júnior, Angolan official
events.amount: CHF 3m fine plus USD 145.6m compensation claim to the Swiss Confederation (as of 2025-01-31). Bribes and gifts to the official exceeded USD 5m. The contracts earned Trafigura about USD 151m.
events.summary: The first Swiss trial conviction of a company: Trafigura was found liable for inadequate controls that allowed more than USD 5m in bribes to an Angolan official in exchange for oil-related contracts, and its former COO was convicted of bribery.

events.type: Corruption and money laundering, Petrobras fuel-oil trades (Lava Jato)
events.status: charged; case reported stalled as of 2024-04-02
events.parties: Two former Trafigura executives (not named on the page opened), a financial operator and a former Petrobras fuel-oil trade manager
events.amount: About USD 1.5m in bribes across 31 fuel-oil trades (as of 2024-04-02 reporting)
events.summary: Brazilian prosecutors charged former Trafigura executives with paying bribes to a Petrobras manager through offshore accounts and cash in Brazil. The case stalled after Lava Jato was dismantled, and the defendants are seeking to have the evidence thrown out.

events.status: investigated (person formally linked to the criminal case; asset freeze ordered)
events.parties: Mario Alejandro B., former legal representative of Trafigura in Ecuador
events.summary: An Ecuadorian judge accepted the prosecutors' request to link Trafigura's former legal representative to the case over bribes paid to Petroecuador officials by trading firms between 2010 and 2023, and barred him from selling his assets.

events.jurisdiction: United States (New York trial of former Vitol trader Javier Aguilar) / Ecuador
events.parties: Trafigura Group, named by former Petroecuador international trade manager Nilsen Arias
events.summary: Nilsen Arias testified that he received bribes from Trafigura, Gunvor, Vitol and Sargeant Marine through the Peré brothers. This was the first public implication of Trafigura in the Ecuador scheme, and Trafigura declined to comment.

events.type: Corruption allegation leading to a commercial ban (Pemex)
events.summary: Pemex's trading arm temporarily banned new business with Trafigura in July 2021, and Mexico's energy minister said the ban on Trafigura and Vitol would last at least until the end of 2024 over corruption concerns. Trafigura 'strongly refutes any allegation or suggestion of corruption'.

events.type: Fraud (trading on misappropriated confidential information), benchmark manipulation, impeding whistleblowers
events.summary: The CFTC found that Trafigura traded gasoline from 2014 to April 2019 using confidential information obtained from an employee of a Mexican trading entity, manipulated a Gulf Coast fuel-oil benchmark in February 2017, and used non-disclosure agreements that impeded whistleblowers. The case was coordinated with a DOJ corruption task force, but the release does not allege bribery.

events.type: Corruption investigation (Pertamina oil import and trading graft)
events.status: investigated (employee named a suspect and reportedly detained)
events.parties: Employee 'MH', business development / sales manager at Trafigura's Indonesian operating company
events.amount: The overall scheme is alleged to have cost the state at least USD 12bn over five years (as of 2025-07-14). No amount is attributed to Trafigura.
events.summary: Indonesian prosecutors named a Trafigura employee among nine new suspects in the Pertamina graft case, and Trafigura said it was providing him with legal representation.

events.type: Bribery of public officials (Jamaica, PNP payment)
events.status: charged (trial ongoing as of 2024-03-06; no verdict found)
events.amount: About EUR 390,000 paid to a party fundraising company (as of 2024-03-06). Jamaican press reports it as J$31m.
events.summary: Dutch prosecutors are trying Trafigura Beheer over a 2006 payment to a fundraising company linked to Jamaica's then-ruling PNP, made on the instruction of a Jamaican minister. The trial began in 2021 and has had long gaps.

excluded_namesakes.name: Vitol (including former trader Javier Aguilar)
excluded_namesakes.reason: A rival trader often reported alongside Trafigura. Its DOJ settlement over Brazil, Mexico and Ecuador bribes and the Aguilar trial are Vitol matters, not Trafigura matters. Only Arias's testimony naming Trafigura is kept.

excluded_namesakes.name: Gunvor
excluded_namesakes.reason: A separate trader named in the same Petroecuador and Brazil coverage. Its settlements and provisions are not attributable to Trafigura.

excluded_namesakes.name: Trafigura Probo Koala toxic-waste case (Trafigura Beheer BV, Netherlands 2010)
excluded_namesakes.reason: Same group, but an environmental conviction rather than bribery or corruption, so it was left out of the events.

output.assessment: High bribery and corruption risk. Trafigura has a US guilty plea over Petrobras bribes (2024) and a first-instance Swiss conviction over Angola (January 2025, CHF 3m fine plus USD 145.6m compensation), and both name Trafigura Beheer B.V. There are also open or unresolved matters in Ecuador, Indonesia, Brazil, the Netherlands (Jamaica) and Mexico. Still open: the Swiss appeal (Trafigura and Wainwright said they would appeal, but I found no appeal ruling or hearing date), the Dutch Jamaica verdict, the Brazilian prosecution, the Ecuadorian case against Trafigura's former representative, and the Indonesian case. Out of scope but worth checking separately: Bolivia's suspension of Trafigura fuel contracts over alleged adulterated gasoline (2026), and the Nyrstar matter in Belgium.
